percentage-calculator.title: Online percentage calculator — CalcHub
percentage-calculator.name: Percentage calculator
percentage-calculator.description: Free percentage calculator: find a percentage of a number, what percent one number is of another, percentage change, and increase or decrease a number by a percentage.
percentage-calculator.intro: Choose a calculation type and enter two numbers: the result appears instantly. Your data is not sent to any server.

percentOf.name: Percentage of a number
percentOf.explain: To find a percentage of a number, multiply the number by the percentage and divide by 100.

whatPercent.name: What percent one number is of another
whatPercent.explain: Divide the part by the whole and multiply by 100.

change.name: Percentage change between two numbers
change.explain: Subtract the starting value from the new value, divide by the absolute value of the starting value and multiply by 100. A positive result is an increase, a negative one is a decrease.

increase.name: Increase a number by a percentage

decrease.name: Decrease a number by a percentage

percentage-calculator.faq1q: How do I calculate a percentage of a number?
percentage-calculator.faq1a: Multiply the number by the percentage and divide by 100. For example, 15% of 200: 200 × 15 ÷ 100 = 30.
percentage-calculator.faq2q: What is the difference between a 10% increase and a 10 percentage point increase?
percentage-calculator.faq2a: A 10% increase changes a value relative to itself: 50 becomes 55. Percentage points are the difference between two percentages: going from 5% to 15% is 10 percentage points, but relative to the starting value it is a 200% increase.
percentage-calculator.faq3q: Why doesn’t a number return to the original after decreasing and then increasing by the same percentage?
percentage-calculator.faq3a: Because the second percentage is calculated from the new number. Decrease 100 by 20% and you get 80; increase 80 by 20% and you get 96, not 100.
percentage-calculator.keywords: percentage percent change increase decrease відсоток procent

discount-calculator.title: Online discount calculator — CalcHub
discount-calculator.name: Discount calculator
discount-calculator.description: Free discount calculator: find the price after discount and the amount you save from the original price and discount percentage.
discount-calculator.intro: Enter the original price and the discount percentage to see the final price and how much you save.
discount-calculator.keywords: discount sale offer price after discount знижка rabatt
discount-calculator.howItWorks: The discount amount is a percentage of the original price. Subtracting it from the price gives the final cost. You can also do it in one step: price × (1 − discount ÷ 100).
discount-calculator.faq1q: How do I calculate a price after a discount?
discount-calculator.faq1a: Multiply the price by (1 − discount ÷ 100). For example, 1200 with a 25% discount: 1200 × 0.75 = 900.
discount-calculator.faq2q: How do I find the discount percentage from an old and a new price?
discount-calculator.faq2a: Subtract the new price from the old one, divide by the old price and multiply by 100. The “Percentage change” mode in the percentage calculator does this for you.

vat-calculator.title: Online VAT calculator — CalcHub
vat-calculator.name: VAT calculator
vat-calculator.description: Free VAT calculator: add VAT to a net amount or extract the VAT from an amount that already includes it.
vat-calculator.intro: Choose what to calculate, enter the amount and the VAT rate to see the VAT, the net amount and the gross amount.
vat-calculator.keywords: vat tax value added tax moms пдв sales tax
vat-calculator.howItWorks: To add VAT, multiply the net amount by the rate and divide by 100: that is the VAT. To extract VAT from a gross amount, divide it by (1 + rate ÷ 100) to get the net amount; the difference is the VAT.
vat-calculator.example: Net 1000 at 20%: VAT = 200, total 1200. In reverse: from 1200 including VAT, 1000 is the net amount.
vat-calculator.faq1q: How do I add VAT to a price?
vat-calculator.faq1a: Multiply the net price by (1 + rate ÷ 100). At a 20% rate, 1000 becomes 1200.
vat-calculator.faq2q: How do I extract VAT from an amount that already includes it?
vat-calculator.faq2a: Do not take the rate of the gross amount: that overstates the VAT. Divide the amount by (1 + rate ÷ 100) to get the net price, then subtract it from the amount. For example, 1200 ÷ 1.2 = 1000, so the VAT is 200.

area-calculator.title: Online area calculator — CalcHub
area-calculator.name: Area calculator
area-calculator.description: Free area calculator: work out the area of a rectangle, triangle or circle in metres, centimetres, millimetres or feet.
area-calculator.intro: Choose a shape and a unit, enter the dimensions and the area is calculated instantly.
area-calculator.keywords: area square meters square feet rectangle triangle circle площа
area-calculator.howItWorks: The area depends on the shape: for a rectangle it is length × width, for a triangle base × height ÷ 2, and for a circle π × radius². The result is given in square units of the length unit you chose.
area-calculator.faq1q: How do I calculate the area of a room?
area-calculator.faq1a: If the room is rectangular, multiply the length by the width. For an irregular room, split it into simple shapes, find the area of each and add them together.
area-calculator.faq2q: How many square centimetres are in a square metre?
area-calculator.faq2a: 10,000. Since 1 m = 100 cm and area is the product of two lengths: 100 × 100 = 10,000.

volume-calculator.title: Online volume calculator — CalcHub
volume-calculator.name: Volume calculator
volume-calculator.description: Free volume calculator: work out the volume of a box, cylinder or sphere and see the result in litres right away.
volume-calculator.intro: Choose a shape and a unit, enter the dimensions and see the volume in cubic units and in litres.
volume-calculator.keywords: volume cubic meters litres liters box cylinder sphere об’єм
volume-calculator.howItWorks: The volume of a box is length × width × height, of a cylinder π × radius² × height, and of a sphere 4/3 × π × radius³. One cubic metre equals 1,000 litres.
volume-calculator.faq1q: How many litres are in a cubic metre?
volume-calculator.faq1a: 1,000 litres. A cubic metre is a cube with 1 m sides, which is 100 × 100 × 100 cm = 1,000,000 cm³, and a litre is 1,000 cm³.
volume-calculator.faq2q: How do I calculate the volume of a cylinder?
volume-calculator.faq2a: Multiply the base area (π × radius²) by the height. For example, radius 0.5 m and height 2 m: 3.1416 × 0.25 × 2 ≈ 1.571 m³.

length-converter.title: Online length converter — CalcHub
length-converter.name: Length converter
length-converter.description: Free length converter: convert kilometres, metres, centimetres, millimetres, miles, yards, feet and inches.
length-converter.intro: Enter a value and choose the units: the result appears instantly.
length-converter.keywords: length converter kilometers miles meters feet inches довжина längd
length-converter.howItWorks: The value is first converted to metres and then to the target unit, using exact factors: 1 mile = 1,609.344 m, 1 yard = 0.9144 m, 1 foot = 0.3048 m, 1 inch = 0.0254 m.
length-converter.faq1q: How many kilometres are in a mile?
length-converter.faq2q: How many centimetres are in an inch?

mass-converter.title: Online mass converter — CalcHub
mass-converter.name: Mass converter
mass-converter.description: Free mass converter: convert tonnes, kilograms, grams, milligrams, pounds and ounces.
mass-converter.intro: Enter a value and choose the units: the result appears instantly.
mass-converter.keywords: mass weight converter kilograms pounds ounces grams вага маса vikt
mass-converter.howItWorks: The value is first converted to kilograms and then to the target unit, using exact factors: 1 pound = 0.45359237 kg, 1 ounce = 0.028349523125 kg.
mass-converter.faq1q: How many grams are in a pound?
mass-converter.faq2q: How many ounces are in a kilogram?

fuel-consumption-calculator.title: Online fuel consumption calculator — CalcHub
fuel-consumption-calculator.name: Fuel consumption calculator
fuel-consumption-calculator.description: Free fuel consumption calculator: find your consumption in litres per 100 km from the distance driven and the fuel used.
fuel-consumption-calculator.intro: Enter the distance driven and the fuel used to see the consumption per 100 km.
fuel-consumption-calculator.keywords: fuel consumption petrol gasoline diesel l/100km mpg litres витрата пального bränsleförbrukning
fuel-consumption-calculator.howItWorks: Consumption per 100 km equals the fuel used divided by the distance driven and multiplied by 100. The inverse is how many kilometres the car covers on one litre.
fuel-consumption-calculator.faq1q: How do I calculate fuel consumption per 100 km?
fuel-consumption-calculator.faq1a: Divide the fuel used by the distance driven and multiply by 100. For example, 31.5 L over 450 km: 31.5 ÷ 450 × 100 = 7 L/100 km.
fuel-consumption-calculator.faq2q: How can I measure fuel consumption accurately?
fuel-consumption-calculator.faq2a: Fill the tank completely, reset the trip meter, drive as usual, then fill the tank completely again. Use the amount of fuel added and the distance on the trip meter for the calculation.

trip-cost-calculator.title: Online trip cost calculator — CalcHub
trip-cost-calculator.name: Trip cost calculator
trip-cost-calculator.description: Free car trip cost calculator: work out the fuel needed and the cost from distance, consumption and fuel price.
trip-cost-calculator.intro: Enter the distance, your car’s consumption and the fuel price to see how many litres you need and what it will cost.
trip-cost-calculator.keywords: trip cost fuel cost petrol gasoline price car journey resekostnad вартість поїздки
trip-cost-calculator.howItWorks: Fuel needed = distance × consumption per 100 km ÷ 100. Trip cost = fuel needed × price per litre. For a round trip the distance is doubled.
trip-cost-calculator.example: Distance 300 km, consumption 7 L/100 km, price 55 per litre: 300 × 7 ÷ 100 = 21 L, cost 21 × 55 = 1155.
trip-cost-calculator.faq1q: How do I calculate the cost of a car trip?
trip-cost-calculator.faq1a: Multiply the distance by the consumption per 100 km and divide by 100 to get litres of fuel. Then multiply the litres by the price per litre.
trip-cost-calculator.faq2q: Does the calculator include other costs?
trip-cost-calculator.faq2a: No, only fuel. Tolls, parking and wear on the car need to be added separately.

loan-calculator.title: Online loan calculator — CalcHub
loan-calculator.name: Loan calculator
loan-calculator.description: Free loan calculator: work out the monthly payment, total repayment and interest cost with annuity or equal-principal payments.
loan-calculator.intro: Enter the loan amount, annual interest rate and term to see the monthly payment, the total repaid and the interest cost.
loan-calculator.keywords: loan mortgage monthly payment annuity interest repayment lån кредит
loan-calculator.howItWorks: With an annuity loan the payment is the same every month: P × r ÷ (1 − (1 + r)^−n), where r is the monthly rate (annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100) and n is the number of months. With equal principal payments you repay the same part of the debt each month (P ÷ n) plus interest on the remaining balance, so payments fall over time. The result is an estimate: a lender’s real terms (fees, insurance) may differ.
loan-calculator.example: Loan of 100,000 over 12 months at 12% a year (annuity): payment ≈ 8,884.88, total ≈ 106,618.55, interest ≈ 6,618.55.
loan-calculator.faq1q: What is the difference between annuity and equal-principal payments?
loan-calculator.faq1a: Annuity payments are the same throughout the term, so interest makes up most of the early payments. Equal-principal payments start higher and fall each month, and the total interest is usually lower.
loan-calculator.faq2q: Why can the bank’s actual payment differ?
loan-calculator.faq2a: A lender may add fees or insurance, accrue interest differently and round payments. The calculator shows a simplified formula-based estimate.

concrete-calculator.title: Online concrete calculator — CalcHub
concrete-calculator.name: Concrete calculator
concrete-calculator.description: Free concrete calculator: work out the volume of concrete for a slab, foundation or screed from length, width and thickness, with a reserve.
concrete-calculator.intro: Enter the slab dimensions and a reserve to see the concrete volume you need in cubic metres.
concrete-calculator.keywords: concrete slab foundation screed cubic meters betong бетон
concrete-calculator.howItWorks: The concrete volume is length × width × thickness (thickness converted from centimetres to metres). An allowance for waste and uneven ground is usually added, typically 5–10%.
concrete-calculator.example: A 6 × 4 m slab 15 cm thick with a 5% reserve: 6 × 4 × 0.15 = 3.6 m³; with the reserve, 3.78 m³.
concrete-calculator.faq1q: How much concrete do I need for a slab or foundation?
concrete-calculator.faq1a: Multiply the length by the width and by the thickness, all in metres. For a 6 × 4 m slab 15 cm thick: 6 × 4 × 0.15 = 3.6 m³.
concrete-calculator.faq2a: Some concrete is lost while pouring and the base is rarely perfectly level. A reserve of a few per cent is therefore added to the calculated volume.

tile-calculator.title: Online tile calculator — CalcHub
tile-calculator.name: Tile calculator
tile-calculator.description: Free tile calculator: work out how many tiles you need for a floor or wall from the surface size, tile size and a cutting reserve.
tile-calculator.intro: Enter the surface dimensions, the size of one tile and a reserve to see how many tiles to buy.
tile-calculator.keywords: tile calculator tiles floor wall number of tiles kakel плитка
tile-calculator.howItWorks: Number of tiles = surface area ÷ area of one tile, rounded up. The reserve (usually 5–15%) covers cutting, breakage and pattern matching. Grout joints are not taken into account.
tile-calculator.example: Surface 4 × 3 m (12 m²), 30 × 30 cm tiles, 10% reserve: 12 ÷ 0.09 = 133.3 → 134 tiles without reserve; with reserve, 147 tiles.
tile-calculator.faq1q: How many tiles do I need for a floor?
tile-calculator.faq1a: Divide the floor area by the area of one tile and round up. For example, 12 m² and 30 × 30 cm tiles (0.09 m²): 12 ÷ 0.09 ≈ 133.3, so 134 tiles without a reserve.
tile-calculator.faq2q: How large a reserve should I take?
tile-calculator.faq2a: Typically 5–10% for a simple layout and up to 15% for a diagonal or complex pattern. This is a rule of thumb: the exact figure depends on the room shape.

paint-calculator.title: Online paint calculator — CalcHub
paint-calculator.name: Paint calculator
paint-calculator.description: Free paint calculator: work out how many litres of paint you need for walls or a ceiling from the area, number of coats and coverage per square metre.
paint-calculator.intro: Enter the area, the number of coats and the paint coverage to see the volume you need and how many cans to buy.
paint-calculator.keywords: paint calculator walls ceiling litres cans färg фарба
paint-calculator.howItWorks: Paint volume = area × number of coats ÷ coverage (how many m² one litre covers, stated on the can). The number of cans is the volume divided by the can size, rounded up.
paint-calculator.example: Area 40 m², 2 coats, coverage 10 m²/L: 40 × 2 ÷ 10 = 8 L; that is 2 cans of 5 L.
paint-calculator.faq1q: Where can I find the paint coverage?
paint-calculator.faq1a: It is usually printed on the can as square metres per litre for one coat. Rough surfaces take more paint.
paint-calculator.faq2q: Does the calculator account for windows and doors?
paint-calculator.faq2a: No. Enter the area you actually need to paint: subtract windows and doors from the wall area.
